life_summary: Neil Loren Andersen was born on August 9, 1951, in Logan, Utah. He grew up in northern Utah during the post-war era and pursued an education that prepared him for both business and ecclesiastical leadership. Before his full-time service in the Church leadership, Andersen developed a successful career while maintaining active involvement in his local congregation. He married Kathy Sue Williams on March 20, 1975, at the Salt Lake Temple, and together they raised their family while he progressed through various Church assignments. His early life balanced professional ambitions with religious commitment, eventually leading him to prioritize full-time Church service and administration.
church_summary: Andersen served as a missionary in France during his youth and later served as president of the Church's France Bordeaux Mission from 1989 to 1992, demonstrating a deep connection to French culture and language. He was called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles in 2014. His ministry has emphasized marriage and family values, including opposition to practices that undermine traditional family structures. He has presided over temple groundbreakings, including the Twin Falls Idaho Temple (2006) and the Gila Valley Arizona Temple (2009). His teaching focuses on the importance of strong marriages and families as foundations of society and personal spiritual development.
